question: to the Commission Wouter Beke (PPE) Subject:

The extension of the EU MRV and EU ETS frameworks to offshore activities constitutes a significant step in the implementation of the European Green Deal. At the same time, stakeholders in the offshore sector note that the practical implementation of the MRV system presents challenges. In particular, the application of key concepts, such as the definition of a ‘port of call’, does not always seem to align well with the operational reality of offshore activities. This can lead to uncertainty and additional red tape. Since the MRV framework forms the basis for the operation of the EU ETS in the maritime sector, these stumbling points may also affect the correct application of the ETS. In addition, attention is drawn to the potential implications for the level playing field with non-European stakeholders. In view of the above: 1.

What is the Commission’s assessment of the applicability of the current EU MRV framework to offshore activities, taking into account the implementation challenges identified by the sector, particularly in light of the implications for the EU ETS?
Is the Commission considering further clarification or adaptation of the framework, and if so, what steps and timeline are envisaged?
How can the Commission ensure the competitiveness of the European offshore sector and a level playing field?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.5.2026) As noted in its replies to written questions P-001316/2026 and E-001335/2026, the Commission recognises the heterogeneous and specific nature of the offshore maritime sector. To address issues raised by operators of offshore vessels, the Commission has already included additional clarifications in the guidance document1 accompanying the Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Regulation2 and the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) Directive3. Furthermore, an offshore workstream meets under the auspices of the European Sustainable Shipping Forum (ESSF). This workstream brings together offshore shipping operators, Member States’ authorities and the Commission to discuss practical implementation matters pertaining to the offshore sector with regards to MRV and ETS obligations. As was also indicated, the Commission is assessing, in the context of the upcoming ETS review foreseen in July 2026, what additional measures and adaptations to the legislative framework may be introduced to further facilitate compliance by offshore operators and ensure a level playing field by preventing market distortion, thus safeguarding the competitiveness of European operators in this important sector.
